content:
Some time ago I removed some bucket imports import Lean from mathlib, and the affected files had a significant speedup. If we could entirely abolish plain import Lean from mathlib, then we could have this benefit in all mathlib files, rather than just a few.

I started this with a PR to Qq last month at quote4#134, where I manually reduced the imports, but hasn't been reviewed so far. We will also have to do the same for Aesop.

Do you agree that this is a good idea, or do we want import Mathlib to include all of import Lean?

Jovan Gerbscheid said:

Do you agree that this is a good idea, or do we want import Mathlib to include all of import Lean?

These two aren't mutually exclusive, if we want import Mathlib to include import Lean then Mathlib.lean can have a public import Lean at the top next to public import Std and public import Batteries.

It would be quite unexpected and likely annoying for downstream users if import Mathlib didn't import everything, including all of Lean.

But for individual files, reducing bulk imports is desirable, and I thought there is something written down somwhere instructing people not to use bulk imports in individual mathlib files:+1:

Jon Eugster said:

It would be quite unexpected and likely annoying for downstream users if import Mathlib didn't import everything, including all of Lean.

I'm surprised you say this. I would not expect import FLT to import all of mathlib -- indeed if it did do this then doc-gen would take twice as long to build and would contain a boatload of e.g. algebraic topology which is currently unused in FLT.
We have a linter for e.g. not importing Mathlib.Tactic; we could also have it lint for import Lean if we like.
But I think we do want the mathlib docs to contains all of Lean as well, given that there is no Lean-only docs.

I wouldn't expect that from FLT either, but FLT is a very specific project where as Mathlib is "the" main library.

Various docs and setups just do a import Mathlib which can then be minimised if you do care about compilation time. For example the instructions for mathlib-MWE's would be one place which needs to be changed from import Mathlib to

import Mathlib
import Lean

My assumption is that a mathematical user unfamiliar with Lean would probably want to have a simple import Mathlib and be ready to go with everything available. They don't want to concern themself with the distinction whether something lies in mathlib, lean4, batteries or some other package

My conjecture is that a mathematical user unfamiliar with Lean is extremely unlikely to want to use any part of Lean which is not imported by Mathlib already :-) How much of Lean does this actually apply to? Is it easy to work out which parts of the core Lean repo isn't being imported by mathlib? I see that lots of people seem to think that importing all of Lean is a terrific idea so I'm clearly in the minority. Should we also import all of Batteries and ProofWidgets and Qq and Aesop just in case? Where do we draw the line? I thought "only import what you need" was how it worked. How much does this increase build times?
The only one from those that we don't import fully in mathlib is ProofWidgets.
